items.summary: lru_cache.cu (cuda::std::semaphore, no ROCm libcu++) not ported.

ROCm 10.1.0 rocm-sdk wheels: libamdhip64, libamd_comgr, hipblas, rocblas, rccl and others link the shared libLLVM.so.24.0git, which is built without -Bsymbolic-functions (readelf -d shows only FLAGS_1 NODELETE). A process that already loaded another LLVM (oneflow ships its own libLLVMSupport.so.17git as a NEEDED of liboneflow.so) gets its LLVM 24 static initializers bound to the LLVM 17 copies: import oneflow aborts with realloc(): invalid pointer in llvm::SmallVectorBase<unsigned long>::grow_pod called from libLLVM.so.24 __static_initialization_and_destruction_0. /opt/rocm 7.2.1 did not hit this (comgr there links LLVM statically). Workaround: LD_PRELOAD the SDK libLLVM.so.24.0git; a project-side fix is linking its own LLVM statically or with hidden visibility.

ROCm 10.1.0 (rocm-sdk wheels), gfx1100 W7800: hipOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor returns 1 for dynamic shared memory between the 64 KiB per-workgroup limit and the 128 KiB per-WGP LDS (MaxSharedMemoryPerMultiprocessor=131072), where CUDA returns 0 for a block that cannot launch. Separately, the launch check compares dynamic shared memory alone against 65536: a kernel with 8 B static LDS launched with 65536 B dynamic is accepted (hipGetLastError success) and the queue then aborts with HSA_STATUS_ERROR_INVALID_ALLOCATION, killing the process, instead of failing with hipErrorInvalidValue as 65544 B does. hipFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, 64504) succeeds and is not enforced. 20-line reproducer recipe in projects/oneflow/notes.md (Validation 2026-10-30, fd94e199a). Port-side workaround: check smem + static <= MaxSharedMemoryPerBlock before choosing a shared-memory kernel.

Upstream oneflow defect, every device and build (CPU too): the native channels_last pooling kernels compute wrong values. Maxpool2dBackwardComputeCLast (oneflow/user/kernels/max_pool_kernel_util.h) indexes dy and indices as src_start + h*src_width + w, ignoring the channel, so max_pool_2d(data_format='channels_last') gradients land on the wrong elements (CPU float32 1x6x6x2 k3: max |dx - torch| 11.3; GPU dilated cases 288/288 wrong in every dtype); avg_pool_2d channels_last forward reads garbage on CPU (7.5e33) and is wrong on GPU float64. A CUDA build reaches these kernels for channels_last max pooling with dilation != 1 or return_indices, and for CPU tensors. Not fixed in the port (not a ROCm issue); the HIP double channels_last route deliberately avoids them by pooling an NCHW view. Evidence: agent_space/pool_one.py and pool_nhwc.py recipes in projects/oneflow/notes.md (porter round 2026-10-31).

ONEFLOW_ONE_EMBEDDING_FUSE_EMBEDDING_INTERACTION=1 rewrites embedding_shuffle -> fused_dot_feature_interaction(_grad) to take sparse_feature/sparse_indices inputs; only the wmma tensor-core kernels implement that input, and they are compiled out on HIP, so the fused op aborts with 'sparse_feature is not supported' (the same CHECK a CUDA GPU below sm_70 would hit for float16). That pass is the only thing that sets skip_last_gather/skip_first_scatter, so the P2P embedding shuffle kernels (ported and validated directly in the 2026-10-31 round) are unreachable from a real model on ROCm until a non-wmma (or rocWMMA, wave64-aware) sparse-feature dot-interaction kernel exists. Default (fuse off) is unaffected.

float64 convolution aborts on ROCm: MIOpen 3.6.1 has no FP64 convolution solver (Find logs 'Unsupported data types configuration: FP64xFP64xFP64' and fails compiling MIOpenIm2d2Col.cpp), so conv/deconv in float64 abort in CudnnConvAlgorithmSearch::HeuristicSearch on any AMD GPU, where cuDNN runs them on CUDA. Fix: a non-MIOpen double path in the HIP build (im2col + hipBLAS GEMM, as oneflow's CPU conv kernels do) for forward, data grad and filter grad. Found in the 2026-10-31 porter round answering the 0b04c09af review; not started.

items.summary: ROCm 10.1.0 SDK, gfx1100 (W7800): hipblasLtMatmul with algo == nullptr returns HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR (6) for every f64 GEMM (COMPUTE_64F, R_64F; 4 shapes from 32x8x16 to 1024^3, TN), while hipblasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic on the same descriptor returns an algo that computes the right result. f32 with a null algo works. Reproducer: agent_space/probe/lt64mm.cpp in the 2026-10-31 gfx1100 validation (notes.md). oneflow's cuBLASLt shim needs a workaround (query the heuristic when algo is null) regardless.

rocBLAS 5.7 (ROCm 10.1) gemm_ex with float16/bfloat16 A/B/C/D and compute_type f32 splits k into chunks of floor((2^30-1)/ld) once ld*k of an operand reaches 2^30 and accumulates each chunk into the 16-bit D with beta=1, so D is rounded ~k/1023 times: at k=2^20 on MI300X the error is 25-50x a single rounding (fp16 7e-3, bf16 5e-2 relative; hipBLASLt 2.8e-4 / 2.5e-3), and the 1025 chunk launches take ~8 ms vs 45 us on hipBLASLt. The guard also fires for small operands (ld*k is not the footprint for a non-transposed B). The split is invisible to ROCBLAS_LAYER. Standalone reproducer in the plan oneflow-gfx942-longk-half-matmul (Results). oneflow works around it on HIP (fork d81b70795, hipBLASLt for these GEMMs). Filing, account and whether to check gfx90a first are for jeff.

gfx942 (MI300X, 2 GPUs over xGMI), fork a12ca99e7: the fused embedding-interaction training harness hangs intermittently (both GPUs 100% GFX, device spin) when ONEFLOW_ONE_EMBEDDING_ID_SHUFFLE_USE_P2P=1 is on with the embedding/gradient P2P shuffles: 3/20 untraced + 1/3 in the round runs + 1/10 traced, at random steps (2, 28, 40, 41 of 50). With id_shuffle P2P off and embedding+gradient P2P on: 0/20 plus 0/6. Traced hang: both ranks' last launches are BarrierAndComputeOut (id_shuffle P2P, e256dab86) then BarrierKernel and EmbeddingShuffleCopyKernel (embedding P2P); the spinning kernel is not identified (ptrace blocked on the host). id_shuffle P2P is upstream's opt-in knob and was never run on gfx942 before. Next: the id-shuffle-only result in notes, then a per-kernel device-side timeout/printf in the two barriers.

items.summary: On gfx1100 (W7800, ROCm 10.1.0) hipBLASLt's heuristic kernel for fp16 GEMMs with COMPUTE_32F and long k (Cijk_Alik_Bljk_HHS_BH_..._MT32x32x128_MI16x16x1_ISA1100) loses accuracy as k grows: (2 x 2^20)(16 x 2^20)^T is 7.1 ulp of fp16 (0.82 ulp at k = 2^16, 3.2 at 2^18), and 1 x 2^20 x 64 is 4.0e-3 relative vs 2.8e-4 for a float-accumulated GEMM. torch on the same GPU gives bit-identical errors. It fails oneflow's test_matmul_long_k on gfx1100. Related cost on the same GPU: an fp16 GEMM with a float D is 8-9x slower than with an fp16 D (lt_floatd.cpp, A^T B, COMPUTE_32F, heuristic top-1, 4 MiB workspace: 4096 x 40000 x 4096 16.2 vs 138.8 ms, 1024 x 65536 x 1024 1.85 vs 14.7 ms; the float-D choice is Cijk_Alik_Bljk_HSS_..._MT32x32x64 against HHS MT256x128x32), and 23-28x through torch (torch.mm out_dtype=float32, 4096 x 20000 x 4096: 367 vs 15.9 ms), so a float-D workaround for the drift is not cheap on gfx1100.

On gfx1201 (Radeon AI PRO R9700, ROCm 10.1.0 SDK, hipBLASLt 1.4.1 = 100401) the heuristic's first algorithm for 16-bit GEMMs with COMPUTE_32F, transA=T, transB=N and a small output (16x2, 8x3, 16x1), Cijk_Alik_Bljk_{HHS,BBS}_..._MT16x16x192_MI16x16x1_..._ISA1201, is wrong for many k above 2^17: fp16 D(16x2) = A^T B is 39 / 86 / 60 / 70 fp16 ulp at k = 163840 / 200000 / 2^18 / 2^20 (0.5 ulp at 2^16 and 2^17, 0.9 at 196608). Not accumulation drift: deterministic, independent of lda and of GemmTuning::setSplitK (which the kernel accepts and honours with a PostGSU pass), and constant inputs sum exactly, so A and B elements of different k are paired. torch a @ b.t() on the same GPU hits the same kernel (64 / 86 / 59 / 64 ulp). Standalone C++ and torch reproducers in projects/oneflow/notes.md (Porter round 2026-11-01, linux-gfx1201, 4423a5fd9). oneflow works around it by never giving hipBLASLt a long-k GEMM on gfx11/gfx12.

Intermittent CUDA-graph replay fault on two gfx1100 GPUs (ROCm 10.1 SDK): in cg_ws3 (54 nn.Graph matmuls over both GPUs, ONEFLOW_KERNEL_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1) the first-captured shape's graphs (17x1023x513, plain rocBLAS, every dtype) on cuda:1, sometimes cuda:0, replay with garbage and the next call fails with illegal memory access 700. PREDATES the long-k work: with the k=1023 graphs replayed first (cg_ws3r1f.py) d9e41753e faults 7/8 and 4e418c9d4 6/8 (p=1.0); the default reverse order hides it (d9e41753e 0/12, 4e418c9d4 5/20). The graphs are already bad before any replay, so the corruption happens during the capture phase. Every single-variable condition still faults at the baseline rate (STREAM_FLAGS=0 3/8, ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=0 1/8, ROCBLAS_DEVICE_MEMORY_SIZE 2/8, tile cap 2/8); one GPU 0/8 (n.s.). rocBLAS handle memory never grows (32 MiB). No faulting address is available (AMD_LOG_MASK is decimal-only; graph kernels log ShaderName only at instantiate; no address in the fault log; no dmesg). Standalone hr/gr 0/20. Owner unknown (rest of the port, oneflow nn.Graph runtime, HIP graphs or a library); no standalone reproducer, nothing filed. Next steps in notes.
